narration:
[curious] You’re Elon Musk, the world’s first trillionaire,
and you’re losing the AI race to a company you co-founded: OpenAI.
Google and Anthropic are beating you, too, and it’s annoying you.
But they don’t know your secret genius master plan.
First, you need an AI company.
So you build xAI.
Now, to train your AI model, you need GPUs.
So xAI builds Colossus, one of the largest AI data centres,
in just 122 days.
That’s barely four months.
Then Nvidia and TSMC can’t make chips fast enough.
You can’t wait around.
You want to move at full speed.
So you announce Terafab, your own chip factory.
[confidently] Now, your AI is starving for training data.
So you strike a $60 billion deal for Cursor,
a software company that people use to build software with AI.
Then you launch Grokbot, an AI agent company,
so regular people can hand over their work to your AI every single day.
Still not enough?
You bought Twitter back in 2022.
It’s a social media platform where intellectual people post their thoughts.
Every post, every reply gives you more data, a megaphone,
and a promotion system for everything you sell, because you control the algorithm.
And you’re not even halfway there.
You need real-world data and images.
So you build a self-driving car company called Tesla,
which captures real-world data from the streets.
Then Tesla builds Optimus 3,
a robot with hands gentle enough to hold an egg,
with incredibly precise motor control.
And every movement it makes gives you even more data.
[serious] Then you hit a wall.
Your AI needs three things that Earth can’t
easily provide at the scale you want: power, internet, and cooling.
So you look at the Moon.
The Moon has no taxes, no politics, no shortage of space,
and it’s only a short distance away.
It takes just three days to travel from Earth to the Moon.
So you start a rocket company called SpaceX, which builds Starship,
a rocket designed to land and fly again.
Now, you need internet to train your AI.
So you create Starlink.
You wrap the planet in your own fleet of satellites, and millions of homes,
ships, and planes connect through you.
You can even build spy satellites for the US government.
And you also bought a solar company called SolarCity and renamed it Tesla Energy.
[thoughtful] Now your own energy company starts building
towards the biggest project anyone could imagine: a Dyson sphere.
Picture the Sun as a giant light bulb.
Almost all its light flies off into space, unused.
Now imagine surrounding it with millions of solar panels, swarming like bees,
catching that light before it escapes.
Up there, the Sun never sets,
and the heat radiates into the freezing darkness of space.
[slight emphasis] Now you’ve won.
But one day, the internet runs out of things to say.
So you open your final company: Neuralink.
A chip that reads directly from the human brain.
And now you can expand your business to Mars, too.
Because, at this point, you already own the Earth.
Like, literally.

metadata.title: Elon Musk’s Secret Plan to Own the Future
metadata.description:
Free guide to this video (steps and every source): https://studio.golidee.com/guides/golide-external-2026-11-18-1639.pdf

What if Elon Musk’s companies were all part of one massive plan? From xAI and Grok to Tesla, Starlink, SpaceX, Neuralink, and a possible Dyson sphere, this video explores how his businesses could connect into one AI-powered empire.

It’s a fast-moving thought experiment about data, chips, robots, satellites, energy, space, and the future of artificial intelligence. How far could Musk’s strategy really go?
